question: Explain how the First-Past-The-Post (FPTP) system can result in a political party securing a majority of legislative seats without winning a majority of popular votes.
options: In single-member constituencies with multi-candidate contests, a candidate only needs a plurality (most votes). If opposition votes are split among multiple parties, a party winning 30-35% of votes in many constituencies can win a majority of seats.
correct_answer: In single-member constituencies with multi-candidate contests, a candidate only needs a plurality (most votes). If opposition votes are split among multiple parties, a party winning 30-35% of votes in many constituencies can win a majority of seats.
explanation: FPTP measures constituency-level pluralities rather than national proportional vote totals.
